title: One typed media model from the probe to every reader
description: Media metadata is untyped JSON decoded with five struct shapes in subtitles, unchecked type assertions in the api, and SDK-required fields filled in after the fact (items/sdk.go): the direct cause of the real-device failures, since nothing knows which fields are required. The scan detects stale DTOs with hand-written JSONB predicates, one per past release.
acceptanceCriteria: One MediaSource type and one MediaStream type are what every writer of a source produces (the probe, the listing of subtitle files beside a film, the mark of an unreadable track) and what internal/playback, internal/subtitles, internal/items, internal/api and, through them, the transcode worker decode media_sources.streams and an item's stored sources into; no other struct shape and no map[string]any or []any holds a source, stream or attachment in their non-test code

Every media source and every stream in an answer carries, non-null and valid for its schema type, each field compat/schema-12.4.json requires (17 of MediaSourceInfo, 10 of MediaStream, Index of MediaAttachment) because the type has it: in an item's details, an item listing asked for MediaSources and MediaStreams, a session's NowPlayingItem, and PlaybackInfo both as direct play and with a transcoding profile

That holds for every element and not only the first: each source's streams, the item's own MediaStreams list, a subtitle file beside the film, and the audio streams a transcode offer adds from the full probe of a film with two or more audio tracks
internal/items/sdk.go's WithSDKFields, withItemSDKFields and their default tables are gone and nothing takes their place: no pass over a decoded or built source or stream adds fields it lacks

With the fill-in gone JS-070's check passes: compat/conform reports no violation in any JSON answer of the differential tier or of the four e2e gates, and jellyfin-sdk-kotlin decodes every answer requests.yaml labels kotlin:

A source stored by the release before this one and not yet probed again (its stored DTO lacks the eight source fields and the stream fields the fill-in used to give) is answered with every required field at a valid value (Protocol File, Type Default, SupportsProbing true, TranscodingSubProtocol http; never an empty string for an enum) in an item's details and in PlaybackInfo, before any scan has run

JS-070's proof still stands: test/differential/acceptance.sh and test/e2e/acceptance_conform.sh put #94 (a required source field on GET /Items/{itemId}) and #95 (a required field on the second and later streams of a transcode PlaybackInfo) back, each alone, in the typed model, each tier still fails naming the route, the JSON path and the field, and no mutation names a file or line that is gone

For a film with a video, two audio tracks, a text, a PGS and an external subtitle track and a font, the sources, streams and attachments of those answers hold the same keys and values in the same order as the build before this change: no key gained with a zero value (a Width or an empty Language on an audio stream, a null where the key was absent), none lost, and never a stored-only field (Fingerprint, FileSize, FileETag, SubPath, SubSize, Unreadable, an attachment among MediaStreams); a difference is allowed only where the new value is what Jellyfin 12.4 answers for the same file
The differential tier passes with no entry added to compat/differences.yaml and no entry given a further request or path; an entry that no longer matches is removed

Each media source stores the integer version of the probe that last wrote it (per source, not per library), and the scan decides to probe an unchanged file again for its age from that integer alone: no query in internal/library/scan.go asks whether a stored stream has or lacks a key

A source whose version is lower than the binary's is probed again at the next scan though its file's size and ETag are unchanged, whatever its stored JSON holds (also one with every key today's predicates look for), and both its media_sources row and the item's stored sources, streams and chapters are rewritten; of three films, two older and one current, exactly the two are probed and the current one is not opened

Every source stored before this change is older: existing rows get a version below the current one from the migration, and so does a row a worker of the previous release inserts during a rolling upgrade without naming the column

It is probed once: after that scan the source has the current version and a further scan runs no tool on it; a probe that fails, a store that cannot be read or a scan cut short leaves the source, its item and its old version as they were, logs the key and the reason, and the next scan tries again, while films already probed stay done

The re-probe for version keeps what is not the probe's: the item's id and watch state, the indexes of the subtitle files beside the film, and a stored keyframe index (not NULL) with its video end, which are not read again

Only a probe raises a source's version: listing its subtitle files again, or a worker marking a track unreadable, rewrites its streams and leaves the version as it was, so an older source whose subtitle files also changed is still probed

What a failed read left unset is still retried apart from the version: a keyframe index left NULL for a copied codec in mkv or mp4 is read at the next scan, and unread image cue points of a Matroska film are read from its head and Cues without a probe

A film copied or uploaded again to a new key with another ETag, whose item's source was stored by the previous release, is still matched to that item by this release's scan and keeps its id and watch state: the content fingerprint of a new probe equals that of the row the previous release stored

No type assertion, single-value or with its ok discarded, on a media source, stream or attachment, or on an item's MediaSources, MediaStreams or MediaAttachments, is left in the non-test code of internal/api or internal/subtitles
